# Shipping orders

Most online orders are small: a pair of mugs, a serving bowl, sometimes a full dinner set. Clay is heavy and fragile, so packing takes more care here than in most shops.

## Packing ceramics

Every piece is wrapped in two layers of recycled paper and then nested in corrugated inserts. Plates are packed standing on their edge, never flat, because they survive knocks far better that way. Boxes are shaken gently before sealing; if anything rattles, the parcel is reopened and padded again. Tom keeps a laminated diagram above the packing bench showing how a twelve-piece dinner set fits into a double-walled box.

## Couriers and collection

A regional courier collects from the studio at three o'clock on weekdays. Anything packed after that waits for the next day. International parcels go through a different carrier that requires customs forms; those are printed together with the shipping label so nothing gets separated on the way.

## Damaged deliveries

If a customer reports a breakage, we ask for a photo of the item and the box within forty-eight hours. Claims are filed with the courier by Tom, and the customer receives a replacement without waiting for the courier's decision. Repeated damage on the same route is logged so we can decide whether to switch carriers.
